transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-11-20 10:00 UTC | Duration: ~72 minutes
Attendees: Asha Menon (CEO), Liam Carter (CTO), Priya Desai (Head of Product), Marcus Li (VP Eng), Sofia Alvarez (Head of People), Diego Ramos (Head of Sales), plus company-wide attendees (recording)

Summary:
Leadership gave a status update on hiring, runway, product priorities (Serving/runtime, Dedicated, Private), and reliability investments. Open Q&A focused on headcount prioritization, enterprise readiness (SAML/KMS/SOC2), and cost control levers (batching, quantization, caching).

Topics covered:
- Company health and runway updates
- Product: roadmap tradeoffs (latency vs cost, Dedicated vs Hosted)
- Reliability and incident follow-ups
- Hiring and org prioritization
- Sales & GTM notes for Dedicated and Private
- Q&A and next steps

--- Transcript body (partial, automatically transcribed, occasional errors):
[00:00] Asha (CEO): alright um hey everyone thanks for joining on time, appreciate it. good to see folks, today we wanted to do a slightly different all-hands — holdfast and forward, short signal, then open q&a.
[00:28] Marcus (VP Eng): quick ops note — last week's outage, thanks to SRE for the triage, we tracked it to an autoscaling loop interacting with an older kernel on the Dedicated fleet, we rolled a mitigation, we're doing a postmortem next week.
[00:45] Liam (CTO): yeah, and just to add, root cause was a resource leak under heavy caching pressure — the KV cache bloomed in some workloads and then the autoscaler flapped, we now have a circuit breaker and better metrics on prefix cache size.
[01:12] Speaker 1 (someone from eng): is the KV cash the same thing as the prefix cache we keep mentioning? i thought that was only on Hosted.
[01:25] Marcus (VP Eng): good q — prefix KV cache is used across modes, there are implementation differences between Hosted and Dedicated but the concept is the same, we need better visibility.
[01:50] Asha (CEO): high level on business — revenue is tracking slightly above plan for the quarter, pipeline for Dedicated accounts is strong, but conversion timing means we need to be conscious about burn. we have runway into mid-2029 assuming current plan, which gives a bit of buffer to invest in reliability and engineering.
[02:20] Sofia (Head of People): hiring update — we approved 14 total headcount this quarter, prioritizing SRE, infra, and a couple senior product roles. we will pause some non-critical IC hires — manager heads should re-evaluate open reqs by next week.
[02:47] Priya (Head of Product): product priorities — top three: 1) reliability and observability (Console improvements), 2) cost controls (Optimize tooling: batching/caching suggestions), 3) enterprise feature parity (SAML SSO, KMS integration, audit trails).
[03:15] Diego (Head of Sales): from GTM — enterprise buyers keep asking about Private and on-prem options plus SOC 2/ISO, and they're comparing us to choir — uh sorry — to Anthropic and OpenAI offerings on SLAs. our differentiated message is predictable inference economics + rollout tooling.
[03:44] Audience (crosstalk): laughing, uh "choir"
[03:52] Liam (CTO): tech note — on the quantization roadmap, Marcus's team is shipping a 4-bit path for several Llama forks, but there are accuracy tradeoffs for certain instruction-tuned variants. we need evals tied to customer prompts before rolling to production.
[04:30] Speaker 2 (Data scientist): can you say more about which evals? perf numbers?
[04:42] Marcus (VP Eng): sure, we have a benchmarking spreadsheet linked in the notes (will share). early numbers show 2-3x throughput improvements with 4-bit on A100s for short seqs, but some hallucination modes tick up on longer chats. we'll run regression suites.
[05:10] Asha (CEO): ok turning to finances briefly — we will be conservative in Q1 hiring and prioritize runway-preserving moves; that said, we won't cut key infra work that protects customers.
[05:29] Sofia (Head of People): managers please update hiring prioritization doc by EOW — the template is in HR drive.
[05:40] Audience: okay
[05:48] Priya (Head of Product): roadmap tradeoffs — we can either push faster on Private & VPC onboarding for a few early enterprise pilots, or invest in cost-of-serving improvements that reduce hosted unit economics for everyone. can't do both at full speed this quarter. thoughts?
[06:20] Diego (Head of Sales): pilots for Private bring larger ARR and faster contract velocity in regulated verticals, but sales needs a tighter SSO/KMS story; if we invest there we expect 6-9 month payback but higher ACV.
[06:45] Liam (CTO): from infra POV, Dedicated and Private share a lot of runtime code, but Private requires more support and hardened install experience. that work also reduces friction for Dedicated but adds a significant implementation surface for on-prem installers.
[07:12] Asha (CEO): decision — priority to reliability and enterprise parity this quarter. we will sequence cost-optimization work as a close second, and defer some exploratory feature bets.
[07:28] Audience (soft applause)
[07:35] Speaker 3 (Support lead): question on observability retention — users ask for longer logs for audits, any change?
[07:46] Priya (Head of Product): yes, enterprise add-on for extended retention is under pricing review; we'll post draft pricing and get feedback from sales.
[08:05] Asha (CEO): quick recognition — shout-out to the SRE team and to Riley in sales for closing a tricky renewal last week, great cross-team effort.
[08:16] Sofia (Head of People): also, culture pulse update — engagement ticked up 4 points from last survey, hiring is still top concern. managers need to run team syncs re: prioritization and be transparent.
[08:42] Q&A open floor:
[09:00] Allie (Staff SWE): hi — curious about the autoscaler change; will we see configuration knobs as part of Console? many teams need per-customer tuning.
[09:18] Marcus (VP Eng): yes, Console will expose some autoscaler knobs for Dedicated tenants; for Hosted we will keep smarter defaults but partners will get more control under Dedicated.
[09:45] Speaker 4 (random): a lot of noise, sorry bad mic
[10:05] Diego (Head of Sales): we also have to nail messaging on cost per token; customers ask for clear comparisons vs self-hosting on GCP and vs other APIs. Priya we need a one-pager for sales.
[10:28] Priya (Head of Product): noted — I'll prepare a customer-facing unit economics one-pager with examples of batching, caching, and quantization tradeoffs.
[10:40] [12:00] Segment: Product roadmap deep-dive (abbreviated)
[12:12] Priya: quick bullets — Console: cheaper dashboards and per-route cost breakdowns, Optimize: ML-driven batching hints, Dedicated: committed throughput with burst, Private: VPC package + simplified installer.
[12:45] Speaker 5 (engineer): will private support HSM/KMS?
[12:55] Liam (CTO): yes KMS/HSM integration is in scope for Private for key rotations and customer-controlled keys, and audit logs will be extended. note: SOC2 readiness work continues.
[13:20] Marcus (VP Eng): timeline note — reliability sprint is next two weeks; expect small surface-area releases to prod for metrics and circuit-breakers.
[13:45] Asha (CEO): we also want to be careful about external benchmarking; Diego please coordinate with research to publish a fair benchmark, not cherry-picked.
[14:05] Diego: will do, we'll use realistic prompt sets and show latency/cost tradeoffs.
[14:18] [20:00] People & org discussion
[20:20] Sofia (Head of People): hiring rubric — we will bias toward senior ICs in infra and SRE, reduce junior hires for next quarter, and freeze some non-critical contractor renewals. managers to update before Friday.
[21:05] Speaker 6 (manager): can we get clarity on leveling changes? there was confusion in eng about senior titling.
[21:22] Sofia: HR will publish clarifications with examples tomorrow.
[21:40] [30:00] Open Q&A — mixed audience questions (recruiting, benefit questions, remote policy clarifications)
[30:28] Employee: question about travel budget for customer meetings next year?
[30:35] Asha: travel budgets will be prioritized for enterprise renewals and critical pilots; general travel remains constrained.
[30:52] [40:00] Short technical Q&A continues — some transcript noise, occasional mislabels
[40:10] Liam (CTO): small note on kernel selection — we're optimizing kernels per model family and sequence distribution; engineers are profiling autotensor scheduling, this should help latency on longer seqs.
[41:00] Engineer: will that affect our hot caches?
[41:15] Marcus: it will reduce pressure because better kernels lower CPU usage for certain ops, indirectly helping cache pressure.
[41:40] [55:00] Closing remarks
[55:10] Asha (CEO): thanks all, tough choices but clear priorities: reliability, enterprise parity (SAML/KMS/audit), and then cost optimization. we will publish the concrete decisions and the manager playbook by Wednesday.
[55:35] Priya (Head of Product): again, roadmap PDF and one-pager for sales to appear in the shared drive by Tuesday EOD.
[55:50] Sofia (Head of People): managers — please run a 30 minute team sync this week to share these priorities.
[56:05] Asha: final question — any objections? silence. ok good.
[56:14] Meeting end, thanks folks.

Links referenced (will be shared in Slack):

- Draft roadmap and slides (shared drive)

Notes on transcription quality: several sections have minor speaker misattribution, occasional homophone errors ("choir" vs "Cohere"), and missing punctuation in rapid Q&A; recording captured crosstalk and some mics were quiet which caused gaps.
